question: Which important Sikh festival is on 5 November 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Nanak Jayanti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guru Nanak Jayanti**, also known as **Gurpurab**, commemorates the birth anniversary of **Guru Nanak Dev**, the first Sikh Guru and the founder of Sikhism.
 
• Guru Nanak Jayanti is celebrated on the day of **Kartik Purnima** according to the Hindu lunar calendar, which usually falls in the month of **November**. In **2025**, it is observed on **5th November**.
 
• **Guru Nanak Dev Ji** was born in **1469** in **Nankana Sahib**, located in present-day **Pakistan**. His teachings emphasized **unity, equality, selfless service, and devotion to God**.
 
• The celebrations typically begin with **Akhand Path**, a continuous reading of the **Guru Granth Sahib**, the holy scripture of Sikhism, for 48 hours.
 
• A day before Guru Nanak Jayanti, a procession known as **Nagar Kirtan** is held, where devotees sing hymns and carry the Sikh flag, **Nishan Sahib**.
 
• On the day of the festival, Sikhs visit **Gurdwaras** and participate in prayers, kirtans, and community meals called **Langar**. The Langar reflects the values of **equality and selfless service**.
 
• The festival is not only celebrated by Sikhs but also revered by people of other communities who follow Guru Nanak Dev Ji's teachings of universal brotherhood and peace.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Guru Nanak Dev Ji's Teachings:**

 
 
• **Equality:** Guru Nanak Dev Ji rejected caste discrimination and emphasized that all humans are equal, irrespective of their religion, caste, or gender.
 
• **Selfless Service:** He encouraged people to engage in community service and help the needy without expecting anything in return.
 
• **Three Pillars:** Guru Nanak Dev Ji propagated three principles: **Naam Japo** (meditate on God’s name), **Kirat Karo** (earn an honest living), and **Vand Chakko** (share with others).
 
 
 
• **Significance of Langar:**
 
 
• The concept of Langar involves serving free meals to everyone, irrespective of their religion, caste, or social status. It is a symbol of **community service** and **equality**.
 
• Langar was initiated by Guru Nanak Dev Ji and has become an integral part of Sikhism.
 
 
 
• **Celebrations Across the Globe:**
 
 
• Guru Nanak Jayanti is celebrated worldwide by Sikhs and others who follow his teachings, especially in countries like **India, Pakistan, Canada, the United States, and the United Kingdom**.
 
• Special arrangements are made at **Gurdwaras** globally to mark this auspicious occasion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Sikh Festivals:**

 
 
• **Baisakhi:** Celebrated in April, marking the harvest season and the founding of the **Khalsa Panth** by Guru Gobind Singh Ji in **1699**.
 
• **Lohri:** Celebrated in January, especially in Punjab, marking the harvest of winter crops and the beginning of the harvest season.
 
• **Holi:** Though primarily a Hindu festival celebrated in March, Sikhs also celebrate it as **Hola Mohalla**, a tradition established by Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s teachings laid the foundation of **Sikhism**, which emphasizes the importance of **spirituality, moral values, and social equality**.
 
• His legacy continues to inspire millions worldwide, promoting **peace, harmony, and universal brotherhood**.
